key_insight: Apparent advantages of real neural wiring can reflect physiology tuning rather than connectivity, and some conclusions reverse under independently constrained physiology.
engineering_relevance: For computational model comparisons, match optimisation effort and independently constrain constitutive parameters before attributing performance gains to structural fidelity.
method: Compare real-wiring physiology transferred to nulls (P1) with separate tuning for each wiring (P2).
Restrict separate tuning to physiology consistent with independent data (P3).
Test robustness using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
evidence_signal: In the mushroom-body model, real wiring beat a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but lost by 0.09 under P3; 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, and held-out runs confirmed the reversal.
watch_item: Failure at imaging-consistent physiology indicates model inadequacy, not necessarily a defect in biological wiring; some other structural claims remained robust.
paper_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
